# Conformance table

<!-- Generated by `npm run conformance` from docs/mechanics-spec.md, src/config and the real simulation. Do not edit by hand. -->

Does every implemented value and measurable behaviour equal `docs/mechanics-spec.md` (research date 2026-11-14, reference build 13.10)? One row per spec value or behaviour. This is the numbers track of design §14.7 (issue #61); the suite is issue #64.

## Summary

| Status | Rows |
|---|---|
| match (value taken from a source) | 211 |
| match (estimate) | 57 |
| match (placeholder) | 15 |
| deviation (reason written) | 6 |
| not implemented | 167 |
| **total** | **456** |

## How to read it

- **match**: the implemented value equals the spec value, and the spec itself sources it (OFFICIAL, DATA, COMMUNITY, DERIVED, or confidence H or M in §7.1).
- **match (estimate)** and **match (placeholder)**: equal to the spec, but the spec marks the number as an estimate (confidence L, ESTIMATE) or a design placeholder (P, PLACEHOLDER). It matches a guess, not a measurement. Tune these by feel and by measuring the reference game, then update the spec.
- **deviation**: the implementation differs. The Note column holds the written reason and where it is being fixed. A differing row without a reason fails the suite.
- **not implemented**: nothing to compare yet. This is not a failure; the row flips to match or deviation when the mechanic lands (the Note column says what is missing).
- **Spec** is the value in `docs/mechanics-spec.md`; **Tag** is the spec's own confidence tag; **Implemented** is the value read from the live `config/` key or measured on the real simulation; **Checked by** says which; the row id is the name of the test in `src/conformance/conformance.test.ts` (`npm test`).

Regenerate with `npm run conformance` after changing `docs/mechanics-spec.md`, `src/config/` or the simulation. `npm test` fails when this file is out of date.
